issues.description: Image bytes pass image.tobytes() but are claimed to be format="RGB" without mode conversion
issues.detail: Gemini returns PNG/JPEG bytes. Image.open() is lazy; calling .tobytes() before .convert("RGB") and before .load() yields raw bytes in the source mode (often RGBA or P), not RGB. The OutputImageRawFrame contract (raw bytes + size + format) will then be wrong: size*3 != len(bytes), and downstream renderers will produce garbled images. Fix: img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(...)).convert("RGB"); frame = OutputImageRawFrame(image=img.tobytes(), size=img.size, format="RGB").

issues.description: Module-import-time mutation of a private SDK attribute (READ_BUFFER_SIZE) is a fragile hack
issues.detail: genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5*1024*1024 reaches into a private namespace at import time, affecting all consumers of google-genai in the process, not just GoogleLLMService. The comment honestly labels it a "temporary hack," which is the right disclosure but the wrong durability. Needs a tracked upstream issue, a version pin guard, and a stated invariant about when it can be removed. Otherwise a future google-genai bump silently breaks image responses.

issues.description: Default model silently changed from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash with no migration note
issues.detail: Changing a default model is a behavior change for every existing caller who relied on the default. The CHANGELOG entry says "Updated default" but states no invariant about cost, latency, token counting, or thinking-budget defaults — and the new code path now has a 2.5-flash-specific thinking_budget branch. Callers pinning behavior implicitly via the default will see different bills and different latencies. Document the migration explicitly or keep the old default.

issues.description: No test, no measurement, no stated invariant for the image branch
issues.detail: The new elif branch is added inside _process_context with no unit test exercising inline_data, no measurement of the 5MB buffer choice (why 5MB? what's the p99 image size from Nano Banana?), and no stated postcondition for what happens when multiple inline_data parts arrive in one candidate (each pushed as a separate frame, no ordering guarantee documented relative to text parts). "Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it" — and here it isn't even proved.

issues.description: "image in self._model_name" is a substring sniff used as a model-class predicate
issues.detail: Disabling thinking_budget when "image" in self._model_name is a stringly-typed dispatch that will misfire on any future model name containing the substring "image" for unrelated reasons (e.g. an "image-understanding" variant that does want thinking). State the invariant explicitly: "image-generation models do not accept thinking_config," and gate on a known set or a capability flag, not a substring.

issues.description: Stray blank line and no literate comment explaining the new image-output contract
issues.detail: A spurious blank line is added after self._http_options = http_options with no functional reason. More importantly, the new image-output behavior — that GoogleLLMService now emits OutputImageRawFrame interleaved with text — is a contract change worth one paragraph of docstring on the class or _process_context. A future reader auditing the pipeline will not discover this from the code alone.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful capability but lands UNDER-AUDITED. The most serious issue is a likely correctness bug: PIL's image.tobytes() is called without .convert("RGB") or .load(), so the bytes pushed in OutputImageRawFrame almost certainly do not match the declared "RGB" format and size. Secondary concerns: a module-import-time poke at a private google-genai attribute (READ_BUFFER_SIZE) with no removal plan, a silent default-model change, substring-based model classification, and no test or measurement for the new image branch. Recommendation: fix the PIL conversion and add a minimal test before merge; track the SDK hack and document the default-model migration in follow-ups.
